BusinessJustification: Document exchange workflow requires compressed file transfer for quarterly regulatory submissions to counterparties. Average 50 files per month during reporting periods.
AlternativesConsidered: 1) Individual file upload — rejected due to volume and time constraints; 2) SharePoint shared links — rejected due to cross-organization boundary requirements; 3) Managed file transfer service — evaluated but not yet approved by procurement
RiskAssessment: Medium — compressed archives may contain executable payloads or obfuscated malware. Risk mitigated by DLP content inspection and Defender for Cloud Apps scanning.
MitigatingControls: DLP policy scans all .zip contents before delivery; Microsoft Sentinel analytic rule monitors archive extraction events; Defender for Cloud Apps session policy blocks nested executables within archives
Notes: Quarterly review aligned with regulatory reporting cycle

BusinessJustification: Regulatory filing portal receives compressed packages from external regulators containing examination documents and audit correspondence. Required for SEC and FINRA examination response workflows.
AlternativesConsidered: 1) Uncompressed file upload — rejected because regulator portal mandates .zip format; 2) Secure email attachment — rejected due to file size limits on encrypted email; 3) Alternative archive format — rejected because regulator specifies .zip only
RiskAssessment: High — externally sourced compressed files from regulatory bodies carry elevated risk of supply-chain compromise. Accepted due to regulatory obligation with enhanced monitoring.
MitigatingControls: DLP policy with enhanced inspection for externally sourced archives; Dedicated Sentinel workbook tracking all regulatory portal file activity; Automated sandbox detonation via Defender for Endpoint before file access; Access restricted to Compliance team security group only
Notes: Enhanced monitoring tier applied per Zone 3 requirements
